reason: M44-D/M44-C only tested urllc via a fixed-ceiling served-throughput sweep at 3600 Kbps (12x native) -- deliberately elevated to find its graded band. Native (1x) was measured only via M44-A's wide-open-ceiling avg_prbs_dl demand ramp, which reads a flat, contaminated 5.00 (the observability-floor artifact this whole re-collection exists to fix), not a real above-floor served-throughput number. No matching data exists at 3UE's actual load.

Never tested at any load between native (1x, only via the flawed avg_prbs_dl) and 12x (M44-D's elevated band). 2x native was not on M44-A's own demand-ramp grid (1x/2x/5x/10x/20x/50x/100x -- 2x exists in the grid but, like 1x, reads the same flat 5.00 artifact) and was never probed with a fixed-ceiling served-throughput sweep.

M44-E2's own fixed-ceiling sweep at native load (4000 Kbps) is a real, above-floor, served-throughput measurement at exactly this aggregate load -- found full health at every tested ceiling 5-25 raw PRB (96.4% served at the 5-PRB floor itself, ~100% at >=9 raw PRB, zero loss/rejection everywhere). This is the single strongest reuse candidate in this audit. Caveat, not disqualifying: M44-E2 ran embb ALONE, not simultaneously with native urllc+mmtc traffic the way M8's 3UE condition does. M44-E4 found a real (if small at native-adjacent loads, since E2b's own finding is that embb's degradation band only appears at 3x native or higher) cross-slice coupling where urllc's presence degrades embb -- some small effect at native load is plausible but unmeasured. Recommend reusing this as the anchor with the caveat stated, not re-running a full sweep, given the very low a priori risk (embb was clean even at the absolute floor, with wide margin before its own real degradation threshold at 3x).

M44-E2's own uncapped wide-open-ceiling demand ramp includes a 2x/8000 Kbps row (mean=16.60 raw PRB, max=21.0) -- this specific reading is NOT contaminated by the observability-floor artifact (embb clears the floor easily, unlike urllc/mmtc), so it is trustworthy evidence that real demand sits well above 5 PRB at this load. But it is an uncapped DEMAND number from a wide-open-ceiling ramp, not a served-throughput-vs-fixed-ceiling sweep the way M44-E2's own native-load Phase 2 sweep is, and it is single-slice, not simultaneous. A short new fixed-ceiling sweep at 8000 Kbps (same protocol as M44-E2's own Phase 2, just extended above its own 5-25 PRB grid since demand here is higher) would close this cleanly and cheaply, reusing M44-E2's own script and discipline.

reason: M44-E1 tested mmtc only at 50x native (2500 Kbps) -- the load M44-A itself established as mmtc's own floor-clearing reference, deliberately elevated because native demand is far too low to move avg_prbs_dl off its own 5.00 artifact floor at all. True native load has never been measured with any above-floor instrument. Strong prior for a trivial full-health outcome exists (E1's own ceiling=5 finding AT 50x already shows ~89% served, zero loss/rejection -- 1x is 50x less demand than a load that already serves cleanly at the absolute floor), but this is an inference, not a measurement, and per this project's own 'never invent a number' standard should be confirmed by a real probe rather than assumed, especially since mmtc's true native traffic is BURSTY (2s-on/6s-off), a temporal pattern M44's own continuous-CBR probes have never exercised at all.
